post.description:
Returns one of three outcomes — branch on `status`:

* `authenticated` — session issued (tokens in cookies, or in the body in bearer mode).
* `mfa_required` — **no session yet**. Call `/auth/mfa/verify` with the `mfaToken`.
* `mfa_enrollment_required` — policy requires 2FA and none is enrolled; the returned session is quarantined to the enrollment endpoints only.

⚑ A wrong password and a non-existent account return the same body **and take the same time** — a dummy Argon2 verification runs on the unknown-user path. Do not build UI that assumes otherwise.

After too many failures the account locks and this returns `423 ACCOUNT_LOCKED` with `lockedUntil`.

**Rate limit:** 20 per 5 min per IP, 10 per 15 min per email

post.summary: Rotate the refresh token and mint an access token
post.description:
Consumes the presented refresh token and returns a **new** one. The old token is dead the instant this succeeds.

### Client requirements (not optional)
1. **Single-flight.** Exactly one refresh may be in flight per client, across all tabs. Parallel refreshes rotate the chain concurrently; the loser gets `409` and a genuinely replayed token is treated as theft, killing the entire session.
2. On `409 REFRESH_IN_PROGRESS` — wait ~200 ms, retry **once**, then treat as signed out.
3. On `401` — the session is gone. Go to login. Do not retry, do not loop.

Permissions are re-read from the database on every rotation, so a role change or suspension takes effect within one access-token lifetime (§5.5.3 step 17).

⚑ Presenting an already-used token is treated as **token theft**: the whole session family is revoked, the user is emailed, and an operator is paged. The response is a bare `401` that never explains why.

**Rate limit:** 120 per 5 min per IP

refreshToken.description: `bearer` mode only. Omit in cookie mode — the `__Host-rt` cookie is used instead.
The NEW token. The one you sent is now dead.

post.description:
Emails (or texts) a 6-digit code and returns a `challengeId` to pass to `/auth/otp/verify`.

⚑ **Enumeration-safe by construction.** A `challengeId` is returned even when no account exists — the response body, status and latency are identical, and no message is sent. A client cannot use this endpoint to test whether an address is registered.

**Client rules**
* Drive your resend countdown from `resendAfter`, never from a local timer.
* Requesting again invalidates the previous code: exactly one code is live per address, so "the last code I received" is unambiguous.
* The code must be redeemed from the same browser and network that requested it — this is what defeats "attacker calls you and asks you to read out the code".

**Rate limit:** 10 per hour per IP; 3 per hour per destination; 1 per 60s

post.description:
Same three-way `status` contract as `/auth/login` — a user with 2FA enabled gets `mfa_required`, because an email code is one factor no matter which endpoint issued it.

Failure returns `401 INVALID_CODE` with `attemptsRemaining`. After 5 wrong attempts the **challenge is destroyed**, not merely the attempt: further tries return `429 CHALLENGE_EXHAUSTED` and a new code must be requested. Show that state instead of leaving a dead code box on screen.

Redeeming a code sent to an unverified address also verifies that address — receiving the code proves control of the mailbox.

**Rate limit:** 30 per 5 min per IP; 5 attempts per challenge (hard)

post.description:
Exchanges a valid `mfaToken` + second factor for a real session.

* **TOTP** — ±1 timestep of drift is accepted, but a code cannot be replayed inside its own validity window.
* **Recovery code** — single use. Using one emails the user and prompts regeneration.
* 5 attempts per challenge, then the challenge dies and login must restart.

`rememberDevice: true` sets a trusted-device cookie, if the server enables it. That trust never satisfies step-up, and dies on any credential change (§5.4.5).

**Rate limit:** 30 per 5 min per IP; 5 attempts per challenge (hard)
